sermon.title: Resurrection Part 1
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: In “Resurrection Part 1,” Pastor David G. Kincer teaches from 1 Corinthians 15:35 on, where Paul answers how the dead are raised and with what body. He follows Paul’s common-sense examples of seeds, flesh and the sun, moon and stars, then describes the supernatural body raised in power, and Jesus as the last Adam who gives life now. He ends with the change at the last trumpet, Jesus’ return, and letting God be God about the end times.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added by hand, and obvious caption errors were corrected; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Where he reads Scripture aloud he often quotes the King James wording (for example “raised in honor”), which differs slightly from the NKJV text shown with each section. Some of the sermon refers to pictures on the screen, such as a tomato plant and seed, which are not visible in the transcript.

chunks.section_question: How are the dead raised, and with what body do they come?
chunks.short_answer: He says Paul explains the resurrection of the dead in great detail starting at 1 Corinthians 15:35, and that Paul saw Jesus personally after He ascended. The two questions are honest ones from people with common sense, he says, like the Sadducees, who knew the body decayed, and Paul answers by calling them “fool,” which means stupid or without reason, and by arguing from common sense and then Scripture.
chunks.text:
We are in 1 Corinthians 15:35. He’s going to explain the resurrection of the dead in great detail here. He saw Jesus personally after Jesus had ascended. I know that he has much more clout, much more understanding, much more truth than any author in this present day. Could that be an amen? And we need to get what Paul is saying in the depths of our heart. Here he starts out in verse 35 by saying, “But some will say, ‘How are the dead raised? And with what body do they come?’” These are two good questions. Now this [unclear] is not like some among you that didn’t believe in truth. This [unclear] are people that have common sense questions about biblical matters that they cannot seem to embrace because they just don’t fit into the natural understanding of the human mind.

All right, so they’re saying, “Okay, we get resurrected. What do we look like when we come out? What kind of form do we have, and what is this?” See, it’s a good question: “How are the dead raised, and with what body do they come?” Excellent question. Just like when the Sadducees and these people that could not understand how you could have life after death. You see, they know the body decayed and went into the grave, and back in those days there were no caskets; you went into the grave and the worms ate you and the body consumed itself and you wound up dust. And so they challenged Jesus by saying, you know, “How can there be a resurrection of the dead when this woman had seven husbands? You know, which husband is going to be her husband up in heaven?” See, they lacked understanding in spiritual things, but they didn’t lack understanding in natural things, and it created questions in them. Are some of you like that? Yeah. So some of us have questions, and they’re honest questions, but watch how Paul answers.

Okay. “Fool.” Fool. Now the word “fool” means several things. It means you’re stupid, you know, and that’s how I feel when I get in the presence of God and He’s talking to me. I feel real stupid, ignorant, same thing. Egotistical: you exaggerate your selfish, self-centered intellect, your own importance, above what is common sense around you. Now that’s good stuff. Now that fits in, you know; we exaggerate our intellect above. And Paul is saying you’re foolish, but also part of the definition of “fool” is without reason or without common sense. He said you guys are missing common sense here. Let’s look at this through common sense. And remember, Paul approaches everything through common sense and then Scriptures. You noticed that in 1 Corinthians, right? And that’s what threw me off for a while. I thought his common sense were Scriptures, when he’s just illustrating things in life, and they may not be in Scripture at all, but they work because they are common sense. Yeah. Okay, how many can say, “Well, okay, I could be without common sense in some of these areas, I could be a fool”? You’re halfway there. See, when we think of ourselves more highly than we ought, we open ourself up to a fall.

scriptures.text_nkjv: But someone will say, “How are the dead raised up? And with what body do they come?”

The same day the Sadducees, who say there is no resurrection, came to Him and asked Him, saying: “Teacher, Moses said that if a man dies, having no children, his brother shall marry his wife and raise up offspring for his brother. Now there were with us seven brothers. The first died after he had married, and having no offspring, left his wife to his brother. Likewise the second also, and the third, even to the seventh. Last of all the woman died also. Therefore, in the resurrection, whose wife of the seven will she be? For they all had her.”
Foolish one, what you sow is not made alive unless it dies.

chunks.section_question: What does a seed teach us about the resurrection?
chunks.short_answer: He says Paul’s first example is plants: a seed has to die before it can live again and produce a body and fruit. He says the seed germinates and comes alive on the inside first, and that is how we start, “on the inside first,” then comes the outward fruit, and every seed gets its own body.
chunks.text:
So now let’s listen to Paul. He’s going to explain the resurrection, how it’s happening and what body do they come up with. “That which you sow is not made alive except it dies.” Now he’s talking about plant seeds. Okay, example number one, he’s going to use plants. He’s going to use human, uh, fleshly bodies, and he’s going to use the celestial bodies, the universe. Example number one: “What you sow, you do not sow that living body that shall be, but bare grain,” naked grain, just the grain, just the seed, “perhaps wheat or some other.” Now you see pictures up here. I have a tomato plant. That’s the body right here, that’s the living body, and it has a stalk and it holds these tomatoes and it produces tomatoes. But to the left of that is a living seed. That seed’s not dead yet.

And see, he’s using common sense. The seed has to die before it can live again and produce a body and fruit, isn’t that right? See, he’s approaching it from a very common-sense approach. Over here on the left is a dead tomato seed that if you put it in the ground, and the right temperature and the right moisture, it will germinate, come alive on the inside first, and that’s how we start, on the inside first. Then comes forth the outward fruit and the body. “But God gives it a body as it pleased Him, and to every seed his own body.” And this is where the evolutionist just can’t figure this out. God made it at the beginning that like kinds produce like kinds; they don’t produce half and half. All right, you mate a snake with a bird, you won’t come up with a flying snake. You won’t come up with anything. It won’t germinate, it won’t work. Got it?

chunks.section_question: What do the different kinds of flesh and the sun, moon and stars show about the resurrection?
chunks.short_answer: He says Paul’s second and third common-sense examples are that all flesh is not the same, and that celestial and earthly bodies each have their own glory. He says the sun, the moon and the stars each have a different look, glory and purpose, and that Paul is using common sense before he has quoted a Scripture, and he applies the first example to evolution and the age of the earth.
chunks.text:
Now, example number two: “All flesh is not the same flesh, but one of flesh of men, of beast, fish, and birds.” Okay, that’s just common sense. We know that horses have flesh, but they’re not human beings; fish have flesh, but they’re not horses. Okay, and if the evolutionist would just use some common sense, they wouldn’t come up with these ridiculous billions-of-years-old nonsense. Every time they come into a problem, they have to make the earth older to solve it. You ever notice that? See, when I was in school, the earth was a million years old, and they made movies on it: 1 million B.C., 1 million B.C. Then they run into problems, so they went to 2 million, 5 million, 10 million, now we’re at 4 billion. Every time they run into a problem, just solve it by extending the age of creation.

“There is also celestial, heavenly bodies, and terrestrial, earthly bodies, but the glory of this celestial is one, and the glory of the terrestrial is another.” Okay, we got the universe up there, we got the earth, the planets, everything, and he goes on to talk about the sun, the moon and the stars have all a different structure, a different look, a different way. All right. He’s just using what? Common sense. See, to these people who have these questions, he’s approaching them first with just common sense. Hadn’t he quoted a Scripture yet? I love this guy. Any educated person that really learned in school could understand this stuff. Any uneducated person who dropped out of school can understand this stuff, isn’t that right? It’s just common sense; you can’t argue with it. Yeah, they’re all different. They’re all different. Now he’s going to, there’s the sun, the moon, the stars, all in one, there’s the moon, the sun behind it, and so forth. They all have a different look, a different glory, a different purpose.

There is one glory of the sun, another glory of the moon, and another glory of the stars; for one star differs from another star in glory.

chunks.section_question: What kind of body will we have in the resurrection?
chunks.short_answer: He says the body is sown in corruption and raised in incorruption, sown in dishonor and raised in honor, sown in weakness and raised in power, and sown a natural body and raised a spiritual body. “Spiritual,” he says, means supernatural, so the body comes out of the grave a supernatural body that does not decay anymore and lives forever.
chunks.text: And then he plainly says, “So also is the resurrection of the dead.” You see, he made his three common-sense examples, and then he says this is the way the resurrection of the dead is. “The body is sown in corruption”: decay. We all know that when you take your last breath, you start rotting. I don’t care how beautiful you kept yourself while you were alive, you start rotting immediately. In three days no one wants to be around you. We’re a decaying people. “It is raised in incorruption,” or eternal, or perpetual, never-ending. You see, “it is sown in dishonor, it is raised in honor; it is sown in weakness, it is raised in power.” Supernatural power is how it’s raised. “It is sown a natural body, it is raised a spiritual body.” The word “spiritual” means not human, not natural, not of the natural things of this universe; it’s supernatural. So the body comes out of the grave a what? Supernatural body that doesn’t decay anymore, that lives forever.

paragraphs.text: And then he plainly says, “So also is the resurrection of the dead.” You see, he made his three common-sense examples, and then he says this is the way the resurrection of the dead is. “The body is sown in corruption”: decay. We all know that when you take your last breath, you start rotting. I don’t care how beautiful you kept yourself while you were alive, you start rotting immediately. So the body comes out of the grave a what? Supernatural body that doesn’t decay anymore, that lives forever.

scriptures.text_nkjv: So also is the resurrection of the dead. The body is sown in corruption, it is raised in incorruption. It is sown in dishonor, it is raised in glory. It is sown in weakness, it is raised in power. It is sown a natural body, it is raised a spiritual body. There is a natural body, and there is a spiritual body.

chunks.section_question: Did Jesus have blood in His body after He rose from the dead?
chunks.short_answer: He says Jesus’ blood drained out when He died, and when He came out of the grave the holes were still in His hands and side but no blood dripped, because He has a supernatural, spiritual body and does not need blood. He says the saints of old who rose with Him came out the same way, since God can get wherever the dust is.
chunks.text: Now here’s Jesus Christ. I used Him because He came out of the grave. His blood drained out, He died, He had no blood in Him. Now He was dead, He comes out of the grave, and lo and behold, the holes are still in His hands and in His side. They’re still there, but there’s no blood dripping out. Why? Because He has a supernatural body now, a spiritual body. He don’t need blood. See, us natural people need blood. The Bible says blood is the life of the flesh. We need that blood circulating through us to get the oxygen and the minerals and the vitamins where they should be so our body functions. But when Jesus rose, see, He didn’t have any blood, and He didn’t have a decaying body anymore. There was a transition in that resurrection, and the saints of old that rose with Him at that same time, they came out the same way. Well, you say, “How in the world? Those saints of old, you know, they went to dust, the worms ate them and pooped them out, and, you know, how does God, how’s that work?” Listen, He can get wherever that dust is. We go back to just a handful of dust. You know, I mean, as big as you are, after a year or so you’re just a handful of nothing. That’s it. Are you there?

scriptures.text_nkjv: Then He said to Thomas, “Reach your finger here, and look at My hands; and reach your hand here, and put it into My side. Do not be unbelieving, but believing.”
For the life of the flesh is in the blood, and I have given it to you upon the altar to make atonement for your souls; for it is the blood that makes atonement for the soul.’

chunks.section_question: Will a sick or frail body be raised as a spiritual body?
chunks.short_answer: He says no matter how frail or sick this body is, it is going to be raised a spiritual body, and a person who accepted Christ and wasted away will be glad, “because certainly you don’t want to come back with that old body.” He uses a person in the last stage of AIDS as his example, and in this section he also makes his own statements about homosexuality, AIDS statistics and government policy.
chunks.text: Now, He came out with a supernatural body, so did the saints of old who rose with Him. Here is a guy dying of AIDS in the last stage of AIDS. You know, the immunity system’s broken down, they’re just wasting away, sores come upon them, it’s a horrible death, and anyone promoting homosexuality is sentencing people to a horrible death. 91% of all people that have AIDS are homosexuals or bisexuals. The rest just happen to get it because their parents, their children and their parents pass it on to them somehow, and blood transfusions and so forth, dirty needles and whatever. But 91%, when you agree that homosexuality is an acceptable lifestyle, you are sentencing people to this kind of death right here, and there is no plague on earth that our government does not quarantine you from except AIDS. Are you looking at me? Yeah, it is sad that 2% of the people in America can have that big an influence on America’s thinking. But anyway, this guy, let’s say he accepted Christ, and I know some that did, and they wasted away. God didn’t heal them and they died. But as frail as this body is, as sick as it is, it’s going to be raised a spiritual body, and he’s going to be glad, because certainly you don’t want to come back with that old body. Amen. You see?

chunks.section_question: Who is the last Adam, and what is the tree of life?
chunks.short_answer: He says Paul writes that the first Adam became a living being and the last Adam became a life-giving spirit, which means Jesus is more than a prophet or a good man: He gives life. He says Adam’s mistake was embracing the tree of knowledge of good and evil over the tree of life, that Jesus is that tree of life, and that you can have knowledge with life.
chunks.text: Now he’s going to go into the spiritual, the Scriptures. This is his style: “And so it is written.” Now where is it written in the Bible, the Scriptures, that “the first Adam became a living being” and “the last Adam became a life-giving spirit”? A life-giving spirit. Wow. Jesus is more than a prophet. Jesus is more than a good man. Jesus gives you life. And you can accept religion if you want to, but I like the life. Adam made his mistake by embracing the tree of knowledge of good and evil over the tree of life. Jesus is that tree of life. And you can get so into the knowledge of God’s Word that you are worthless; you’re just a proud person throwing Scriptures out that you don’t even know. But you can get that knowledge with life, and that life comes from Jesus Christ. All right, the Scripture, Genesis 2:7, “God formed man out of the dust of the ground and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life, and man became a living soul,” or living being. It says here in Corinthians, you see, that’s the first Adam. Now the last Adam, Jesus, is a life-giving Spirit.

scriptures.text_nkjv: And so it is written, “The first man Adam became a living being.” The last Adam became a life-giving spirit.
And the LORD God formed man of the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living being.

chunks.section_question: Do we have to wait for the end time to be resurrected and have life?
chunks.short_answer: He says no: there are two kinds of deaths, so “I don’t have to wait to die and be resurrected at the end time to find life.” We were dead in trespasses and sin, and when we come to Jesus He resurrects us and makes us alive, forgiving all trespasses, which is why anyone in Christ is a new creature.
chunks.text:
For as the Father, in John 5:21, raises the dead. Who raises the dead? The Father. See, you can’t get away from this plurality, Godhead, that is one, all through the Scriptures. You can’t get away from the fact that there’s a plurality in the Godhead, yet that the God is what? One God. “Raised us from the dead, and even so the Son gives life to whom He will.” The Father raises the dead and gives those dead life, and Jesus raises the dead and gives life to whom He wills. So we’re talking about two kinds of deaths here. Do you see that? See, I don’t have to wait to die and be resurrected at the end time to find life. I can die now, and Jesus will resurrect me and give me what? Life. Okay, are you watching this? Are you ready for this?

Colossians 2:13, Paul said, “You being dead in your trespasses and the uncircumcision of your flesh, He has” what? Made alive. See, He gave you life. “He has made alive together with Him, having forgiven you” what? Of a few sins? All sins, all trespass, all break. Trespass means you violated the law. Doesn’t matter if it’s one or 100, He forgives you of all. You see, so Jesus, so we were dead in what? Trespasses and sin. We come to Jesus and He what? Resurrects us. That’s why the Bible says, “If any man be in Christ, he is a new creature; old things are passed away, behold, all things are made new.” Why? He resurrected us out of trespasses and sin, which we were dead in. Got it? It’s powerful. See.

chunks.section_question: What does “we shall not all sleep, but we shall all be changed” mean?
chunks.short_answer: He says we are in the kingdom now, but there is a time when it will be a real thing ruling the earth, and flesh and blood cannot inherit that. “Sleep” means die, and the Bible uses it because we do not stay in the grave: whether sinner or saint it is a temporary period. Those in the grave will come out with a new spiritual body, and those alive will be changed “in a moment and a twinkling of an eye at the last trumpet.”
chunks.text:
In this revealed kingdom that’s coming, we are in the kingdom, don’t get me wrong. We are in the kingdom, but there is a time when that kingdom is going to be a real thing in the earth and not just in our hearts. It’s going to be ruling the earth. Okay, so flesh and blood can’t inherit that, “nor does corruption, decay, inherit incorruption,” or eternity. I’m going to tell you a secret, Paul says, a hidden secret. I’m going to tell you something nobody else knows. I was called to the third heaven, and I know something you don’t know. Well, he got my attention when I read that: “We shall not all sleep.” What’s the other word for sleep? Die. Why does he use the word “sleep”?

Because we don’t stay in that grave, folks. Whether you are a sinner or a saint, that’s a temporary period of time. You’re going to come out, just like people wake out of their sleep. So the Bible uses the word “sleep” for death a lot, because it explains that we are in the ground temporarily; we’re only dead physically temporarily. Got it? Now, “but we shall all be changed”: those that are in the grave come out, spiritual body, a new body, no flesh, no blood, no decaying flesh, I should say. “We who are alive”: there’s a group of people going to be alive. Now let me tell you, we who are alive are going to be changed just like those in the grave came out of the grave. We’re going to be, only we’re not going to die, we’re going to be changed just like that, faster than I can snap my finger, bam, your blood’s gone, your skin is changed, you have an eternal body now. Jesus is going to do it all.

faqs.question: Why does he trust Paul’s explanation of the resurrection?
faqs.answer: He says Paul saw Jesus personally after Jesus had ascended, so he has “much more clout, much more understanding, much more truth than any author in this present day.”

faqs.question: Why did the Sadducees question the resurrection?
faqs.answer: He says they knew the body decayed and went into the grave, so they asked Jesus whose husband a woman with seven husbands would be in heaven. “They lacked understanding in spiritual things, but they didn’t lack understanding in natural things.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: The same day the Sadducees, who say there is no resurrection, came to Him and asked Him, saying: “Teacher, Moses said that if a man dies, having no children, his brother shall marry his wife and raise up offspring for his brother. Now there were with us seven brothers. The first died after he had married, and having no offspring, left his wife to his brother. Likewise the second also, and the third, even to the seventh. Last of all the woman died also. Therefore, in the resurrection, whose wife of the seven will she be? For they all had her.”

faqs.question: What does “fool” mean in 1 Corinthians 15:36?
faqs.answer: He says it can mean stupid or ignorant, egotistical (exaggerating your selfish, self-centered intellect and your own importance), and without reason or common sense. He adds that when we think of ourselves more highly than we ought, “we open ourself up to a fall.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: Foolish one, what you sow is not made alive unless it dies.

faqs.question: Does Paul argue from common sense or from Scripture?
faqs.answer: He says Paul approaches everything through common sense and then Scriptures, and that it threw him for a while because he thought Paul’s common sense were Scriptures when Paul was just illustrating things in life that work.

faqs.question: Why does he say a seed has to die?
faqs.answer: He says the seed has to die before it can live again and produce a body and fruit, and that a dead seed put in the ground with the right temperature and moisture will germinate and come alive on the inside first.

scriptures.text_nkjv: Foolish one, what you sow is not made alive unless it dies. And what you sow, you do not sow that body that shall be, but mere grain—perhaps wheat or some other grain. But God gives it a body as He pleases, and to each seed its own body.

faqs.question: What does he say about evolution and the age of the earth?
faqs.answer: He says evolutionists keep extending the age of the earth every time they run into a problem, from a million years when he was in school to “4 billion” now, and that if they used common sense they would not come up with it. He also says God made like kinds produce like kinds.

faqs.question: What does “spiritual body” mean?
faqs.answer: He says the word “spiritual” means not human, not natural, not of the natural things of this universe; it is supernatural.

faqs.answer: He says God can get wherever that dust is, and that the saints of old who rose with Jesus came out with a supernatural body the same way He did.

faqs.answer: He says yes, and that the biggest example in the Bible is the Pharisees and the Sadducees, who could quote Scripture, preach and make converts yet would not obey, and Jesus told them they would be punished too.

scriptures.text_nkjv: and to give you who are troubled rest with us when the Lord Jesus is revealed from heaven with His mighty angels, in flaming fire taking vengeance on those who do not know God, and on those who do not obey the gospel of our Lord Jesus Christ. These shall be punished with everlasting destruction from the presence of the Lord and from the glory of His power,

faqs.question: Can we put the end-time events on a chart?
faqs.answer: He says no: “these people that try to put all their little charts together are way off,” and when he tried to put his chart together, “ain’t no chart.” God will reveal it when He does it.
